best-broadway-shows.intro:

As Broadway heads into spring 2026, the season offers an impressive range of theatrical experiences, from long-running cultural phenomena to fresh critical darlings. This month's top-rated shows average an 84/100 critic score, reflecting a particularly strong lineup that spans groundbreaking new works and beloved revivals.

**Hamilton** continues its remarkable run as the highest-rated show on Broadway, with critics still praising Lin-Manuel Miranda's revolutionary hip-hop musical nearly eleven years after its debut. The show's 90/100 score across 42 reviews confirms its status as an enduring masterpiece that continues to resonate with audiences and critics alike.

Among newer productions, **Maybe Happy Ending** stands out as a critical favorite, earning an 85/100 rating for its unexpectedly moving story about two robots finding connection. Critics describe it as one of Broadway's most original musicals in recent years, proving that inventive storytelling still has a place on the Great White Way.

**Oh, Mary!** rounds out the top tier with Cole Escola's absurdist take on Mary Todd Lincoln earning enthusiastic reviews for its riotous comedy. The show's 84/100 score reflects critics' embrace of its irreverent humor and bold creative vision.

The diversity of this month's top ten—from the spectacular puppetry of **The Lion King** to the folk-opera stylings of **Hadestown** and the satirical edge of **The Book of Mormon**—demonstrates Broadway's continued ability to offer something for every theatrical taste. Whether you're seeking innovative new voices or time-tested favorites, March 2026 presents an opportune moment to experience Broadway at its most varied and accomplished.

best-broadway-plays.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays: March 2026

As Broadway heads into the spring season, the landscape of straight plays offers a mix of audacious comedy, magical spectacle, and familiar franchises adapted for the stage. With an average critic score of 75 out of 100 across our featured productions, this month's selections reveal an industry leaning heavily into visual spectacle and recognizable intellectual property, though one original comedy stands notably above the rest.

**Oh, Mary!** emerges as the clear critical favorite, with Cole Escola's absurdist reimagining of Mary Todd Lincoln as a cabaret-obsessed narcissist earning widespread acclaim for its riotous humor and bold irreverence. The production demonstrates that original voices can still break through on Broadway when they offer a sufficiently distinctive vision.

Meanwhile, **Harry Potter and the Cursed Child** continues to impress critics with its technical achievements and magical stagecraft, even as reviewers remain divided on the narrative itself. The production exemplifies Broadway's current appetite for immersive theatrical experiences that prioritize spectacle alongside storytelling.

**Stranger Things: The First Shadow** follows a similar pattern, garnering praise for its special effects and technical execution while facing criticism for its three-hour runtime and overstuffed prequel narrative. **Every Brilliant Thing**, featuring Daniel Radcliffe in an intimate interactive format, rounds out the offerings with a more modest production that critics find earnest but not entirely successful.

This month's slate suggests Broadway audiences seeking the most critically acclaimed experience should gravitate toward comedy, while those drawn to visual spectacle have multiple options that deliver on technical ambition, if not always narrative coherence. Consider your priorities—laughs or illusions—before booking your tickets.

Close behind, **Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across New York)** surprises as the month's sleeper hit. Rounding out the month, Daniel Radcliffe headlines **Every Brilliant Thing**, though the interactive play's single review suggests critics find the material earnest but not entirely successful, despite the draw of its marquee name.

Whether you're drawn to epic American storytelling, intimate romantic comedy, or the spectacle of a classic musical chess match, March's Broadway offerings provide varied entry points for different theatrical tastes.

best-broadway-shows-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway shows that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of theater cut short by unprecedented circumstances. These five productions—ranging from bold reimaginings of classics to powerful new voices finally reaching Broadway—offer a glimpse of what that season promised before the pandemic shuttered theaters that spring.

Leading our selections is a grittier reboot of **Les Misérables** at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre, earning an 83/100 from critics who largely embrace its darker vision, even as some remain unconvinced by the departure from tradition. Close behind, **A Soldier's Play** stands as one of the season's most significant achievements—Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama finally received its long-overdue Broadway premiere in a stellar revival that proves the work's examination of race and power within the military remains devastatingly relevant.

The season's other offerings present a mixed but intriguing landscape. **Grand Horizons** delivers boulevard comedy elevated by performances from Jane Alexander and James Cromwell, while **My Name is Lucy Barton** showcases Laura Linney's luminous solo performance in an adaptation that divides critics on its theatrical effectiveness. Perhaps most controversial is Ivo van Hove's radical **West Side Story** reimagining, which polarizes reviewers with its visceral approach and striking video design.

With an average critic score of 75/100 across these five productions, the 2020 season demonstrated Broadway's ongoing tension between reverence and reinvention, between classic revivals and essential stories finally getting their due. For theatergoers interested in this pivotal moment in Broadway history, these productions offer essential viewing that captures both the artistic ambitions and cultural conversations of their time.

Whether you're drawn to intimate character studies like "Clyde's," epic historical dramas like "The Lehman Trilogy," or the pop-infused exuberance of "SIX," the class of 2021 offers something for every theatergoer. best-broadway-shows-2022.intro:

**A Strange Loop**, Michael R. Jackson's groundbreaking meta-musical, captured both the Pulitzer Prize and Tony Award for Best Musical while pushing boundaries with its unflinchingly honest narrative. best-broadway-plays-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of theater interrupted—a season cut dramatically short by the pandemic, yet one that managed to deliver several noteworthy productions before the shutdown.

Among the five plays from that truncated year, **Les Misérables** leads our rankings with an 83/100 critic score. This grittier reboot at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre earns praise for its fresh approach to the classic material, though the reimagining doesn't win over all traditionalists. Close behind, **A Soldier's Play** stands out as perhaps the most significant theatrical event of early 2020, bringing Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama to Broadway for the first time in a critically acclaimed revival that proves the work's examination of race and identity remains urgently relevant.

The remaining productions offer varied experiences: **Grand Horizons** delivers familiar but well-crafted boulevard comedy elevated by powerhouse performances from Jane Alexander and James Cromwell, while **My Name is Lucy Barton** showcases Laura Linney in a polarizing solo adaptation that critics agree features luminous acting, even when they question the theatrical adaptation itself. Rounding out the list, Ivo van Hove's **West Side Story** proves the most divisive entry, with its radical reimagining earning both passionate advocates and fierce detractors.

With an average critic score of 75/100 across these five productions, the 2020 Broadway play season—though brief—demonstrated both the enduring power of classic revivals and theater's capacity for bold reinterpretation. Explore our detailed reviews to discover which of these productions might still resonate with your theatrical tastes.

best-broadway-plays-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2021

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2021 represent a watershed moment for American theater. These productions marked not just the industry's post-pandemic reopening, but a creative renaissance that pushed theatrical boundaries in unexpected directions.

The standout among this exceptional class is *Dana H.*, Lucas Hnath's unconventional docudrama that continues to provoke discussion with its innovative use of lip-sync performance. Deirdre O'Connell's mesmerizing portrayal of the playwright's mother recounting her harrowing kidnapping earns the highest critical marks (86/100) for its unforgettable theatrical daring. Equally inventive is *Is This a Room*, which transforms a verbatim FBI transcript into pulse-pounding drama, proving that documentary theater can be as gripping as any thriller.

The year also saw Broadway welcome back grand-scale productions, with *The Phantom of the Opera* reminding audiences why Andrew Lloyd Webber's mega-musical endured for decades, while *The Lehman Trilogy* delivered an epic examination of American capitalism through extraordinary performances and visionary direction. Meanwhile, *Pass Over* earned its place as Broadway's symbolic reopening show, blending Beckett with biblical allegory to create urgent contemporary drama.

From Ruben Santiago-Hudson's virtuosic solo turn in *Lackawanna Blues* to Rebecca Frecknall's immersive *Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club* transformation, from Marianne Elliott's gender-swapped *Company* to the pop-powered exuberance of *SIX*, these ten productions average an impressive 81/100 critical score. Lynn Nottage's *Clyde's* rounds out the list with its warm-hearted exploration of redemption in a truck-stop kitchen.

Whether you're discovering these shows for the first time or revisiting critical favorites, this guide offers a comprehensive look at the plays that helped rebuild Broadway.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2022

As we look back from March 2026, the 2022 Broadway season stands out as a remarkable year that brought both innovative new voices and essential revivals to the stage. Four years later, many of these productions continue to resonate with audiences and influence the theatrical landscape.

The season's standout is **Kimberly Akimbo**, David Lindsay-Abaire and Jeanine Tesori's quirky musical about a teenager with a rare aging condition. Critics consistently praise its rare ability to balance sharp comedy with genuine emotional depth, earning it the highest marks of the year. Close behind, **Into the Woods** offers a stripped-down revival that serves as a fitting tribute to Stephen Sondheim, while **A Strange Loop**, Michael R. Jackson's Pulitzer Prize-winning meta-musical, breaks new ground with its brazenly original exploration of a Black gay artist's inner life.

The 2022 season proved particularly notable for bringing Pulitzer Prize-winning works to Broadway audiences. Beyond *A Strange Loop*, the year featured revivals of Suzan-Lori Parks' **Topdog/Underdog** and Paula Vogel's **How I Learned to Drive**, alongside new productions of Stephen Adly Guirgis's **Between Riverside and Crazy** and Martyna Majok's **Cost of Living**. Tom Stoppard contributed **Leopoldstadt**, his deeply personal meditation on Jewish identity and the Holocaust, while Jordan E. Cooper's **Ain't No Mo'** delivered provocative satire.

With an impressive average critic score of 83 out of 100 across these ten productions, the 2022 season demonstrated Broadway's capacity for both entertainment and artistic ambition. Whether you're discovering these shows for the first time or revisiting familiar favorites, this collection represents some of the most critically acclaimed theatrical experiences of the decade.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2023

As of March 2026, the plays that debuted on Broadway in 2023 continue to demonstrate the enduring power of theatrical storytelling, with several productions maintaining their critical acclaim and cultural relevance nearly three years after their premieres.

The year proved exceptional for both classic revivals and bold new works, with the featured productions averaging an impressive 82/100 critic score. Leading the field is Maria Friedman's revelatory staging of **Merrily We Roll Along**, which finally unlocked the emotional core of Sondheim's previously troubled musical, transforming it from notorious flop to triumph. The production's success represents one of the most significant theatrical rehabilitations in recent Broadway history.

Contemporary works also made their mark, with **Appropriate** emerging as a modern masterpiece—Branden Jacobs-Jenkins's searing family drama, powered by Sarah Paulson's performance, continues to resonate with audiences grappling with inheritance, both material and moral. Meanwhile, **Stranger Things: The First Shadow** proved that commercially-driven properties could achieve genuine theatrical artistry, with its technically stunning production transcending mere fan service.

The 2023 season also brought timely revivals that spoke directly to contemporary concerns. **Purlie Victorious** demonstrated the enduring relevance of Ossie Davis's 1961 satire, while the revival of **Parade** found urgent new resonance in its exploration of prejudice and justice. Solo performances flourished as well, with **Just for Us** and **Prima Facie** showcasing the power of individual storytelling to illuminate larger social issues.

Whether you're drawn to reimagined classics, innovative new voices, or technically ambitious spectacles, these productions represent some of the finest theatrical achievements of their year—and several continue to reward audiences today.

best-broadway-plays-2024.intro:

As Broadway moves deeper into 2026, the shows that premiered in 2024 continue to demonstrate remarkable staying power and critical acclaim. This collection of ten productions—averaging an impressive 84/100 critic score—represents some of the most innovative and well-crafted theater currently on offer.

Leading the field is **Stereophonic** (88/100), David Adjmi's meticulously crafted drama about a 1970s rock band in the studio. Critics consistently praise its authentic portrayal of the creative process and its theatrical ambition, cementing its status as one of the decade's defining productions. Close behind, **Operation Mincemeat** (86/100) brings grassroots energy and inventive storytelling to Broadway after its West End success, while the ballroom-infused reimagining **CATS: The Jellicle Ball** (86/100) transforms the familiar Andrew Lloyd Webber musical into something entirely fresh and liberating.

More traditional fare also excels: Audra McDonald brings a fresh interpretation to Mama Rose in **Gypsy** (83/100), and a lavish **Oliver!** revival (82/100) balances spectacle with Dickensian grit.

From intimate character studies like **Mary Jane** to innovative dance-theater hybrids like **Illinoise**, these 2024 debuts showcase Broadway's continued commitment to both artistic experimentation and theatrical excellence. Whether you're seeking bold reimaginings or emotionally resonant storytelling, this collection offers essential viewing for any theater enthusiast.

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in 2025

As March 2026 arrives, the Broadway season that began in 2025 continues to resonate with audiences and critics alike, offering a remarkably diverse slate of productions that range from classic American drama to innovative new works.

Leading the field is Ivo van Hove's minimalist revival of **All My Sons**, which earns the highest critical marks with its emotionally intense approach to Arthur Miller's classic. The production's stripped-down aesthetic allows the ensemble cast to deliver performances that critics describe as devastating and essential. Not far behind, the 20th-anniversary revival of **The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee** proves that the quirky musical comedy has lost none of its charm, with critics praising both its airtight writing and its surprising emotional depth.

Family-friendly fare finds strong representation in **Paddington The Musical**, where technical artistry meets heartwarming storytelling through a remarkably lifelike puppet that critics call a theatrical marvel. Meanwhile, serious drama thrives in multiple forms: Sanaz Toossi's Pulitzer-winning **English** brings sensitive exploration of language and identity to the stage, while Branden Jacobs-Jenkins' **Purpose** delivers another of his signature family dramas with characteristic sharp humor.

The season also showcases ambitious new musicals like **Dead Outlaw**, David Yazbek's darkly comic rock score about a bizarre true story, and timely revivals including **Ragtime**, powered by Joshua Henry's acclaimed performance. With an average critical score of 84/100 across these ten productions, the 2025 Broadway season demonstrates both artistic ambition and consistent quality.

Whether you're drawn to intimate drama, spectacular stagecraft, or innovative musical theater, this season offers compelling reasons to experience live theater at its finest.

best-broadway-plays-2026.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2026

March 2026 brings a modest start to the year for new Broadway plays, with only a handful of productions opening their doors so far. While the season is still young, early arrivals offer audiences a mix of intimate storytelling and star-powered draws.

**Every Brilliant Thing** leads the year's debuts, bringing Duncan Macmillan's one-person show about depression, resilience, and finding joy in life's small moments to Broadway. Daniel Radcliffe takes on the demanding role in this interactive production that invites audience participation throughout its runtime. Critics acknowledge the play's sincere intentions and Radcliffe's commitment to the material, though reviews suggest the execution doesn't fully capitalize on the script's emotional potential. The production earns recognition more for its accessible approach to mental health themes and Radcliffe's star appeal than for breaking new theatrical ground.

With an average critic score of 66 out of 100 for new plays this year, the 2026 season is off to a measured start. The limited number of openings through March reflects the typical pattern of Broadway's first quarter, when producers often wait for the post-holiday theater market to stabilize before launching major productions.

As spring approaches, theatergoers can expect a fuller slate of new plays to arrive in the coming months, potentially elevating the year's overall artistic profile. For now, those seeking new dramatic work on Broadway will find options centered on intimate, character-driven storytelling. Check back regularly as more productions open and the 2026 theatrical landscape takes fuller shape.
